summary: Bake the talking-head camera onto the clean cut: a rect-keyframe crop trajectory rendered to pixels (GPU libplacebo, CPU-static fallback).

parity.note: The SHOT is JUDGEMENT and never crosses (detect_track / head_geometry / plan_shots / plan_punches decide it on the brain); only the rect keyframes it emits cross as params, and this op turns them into pixels. Two reasons it is not bit_exact. (1) Since MISC-141 the keyframes are ONE pair per shot (its own start/end rect) with interp:cos — camera_apply/podagent bake `0.5-0.5*cos(PI*p)` between them, reproducing the planner's ease_cos exactly on a no-punch ramp; a punch's fast attack/release (its bump is linear in time, not cosine) is where the bake diverges most from the true reciprocal-zoom curve (measured worst ~0.034 of the frame, tests/test_head_trajectory.py). Trajectories persisted before this change still carry interp:linear over a dense 0.1s-step grid and still bake (the branch was not removed). (2) The primary render is GPU libplacebo on BOTH local and pod (the dev box and the rented pod both have Vulkan), so those two agree structurally — the crop filtergraph is pinned BYTE-EQUAL to the pod's rect renderer (podagent.render._gpu_crop) in the engine's parity suite — but a Vulkan-less box (driverless CI) falls back to a STATIC crop at the first keyframe, exactly as podagent.render._cpu_crop does in the final composite; that fallback is declared, not hidden. Tolerance for the GPU-vs-GPU path: PSNR >= 40 dB / SSIM >= 0.99 frame-to-frame is the intended bar (dominated by encoder quantisation, not geometry); UNPROVEN in a CPU-only environment with no GPU to run a real libplacebo render, so only the filtergraph STRINGS are pinned.

keyframes.description: The camera trajectory as DATA: per-frame crop rects in SOURCE fractions, emitted by head_trajectory.trajectory_for_keeps. Because cover is a uniform scale, a cover fraction IS a source fraction, so each rect applies straight to iw/ih (podagent.render.anim_expr, the SAME renderer the preview uses). Times are seconds on the segment clock.

rect.description: [x, y, w, h] crop window, each in [0,1].

interp.description: How adjacent keyframes are eased. Since MISC-141 the planner emits `cos` (0.5-0.5*cos(PI*p)) — a shot's own two boundary keyframes reproduce its ease_cos ramp exactly, no dense sampling needed; `linear` is kept for trajectories persisted before this change and for the other eased overlay presets that still use this enum.

encode_profile.description: Named quality tier, NOT encoder flags. head_dyn.mp4 is an INTERMEDIATE re-encoded downstream, so `final` runs a high-quality cq (14) to limit compounding generation loss; `preview` trades quality for the 720x1280 proxy. The nvenc/libx264 ladder is tuning and stays in the handler (scripts/render_profile.py is the same SSOT pattern).
